latest_release.name: v0.1.3
latest_release.body:
## Highlights

- Split training data preparation into record-to-record, record-to-task, and task-to-batch stages (#766).
- Add OPD recipes, generated-task training, and AutoEnvScaling examples (#683, #707, #755, #790, #791).
- Let recipes choose the training method for each job (#695).
- Support Slime weight publication to vLLM through the disk transport (#710).
- Share sandbox execution through Harbor environments (#803).
- Fix interrupted training recovery, engine startup port conflicts, relative artifact work directories, and OpenRouter web-search streams (#728, #730, #723, #712, #769).

## Upgrade notes

This release changes configuration and extension interfaces.

- Use the public configuration sections. Remove `schema-version`; legacy layouts, custom service definitions, and `execution.services` are no longer accepted (#782).
- Update composite recipe components to use the `implementation`, `config`, and `runtime` recipe shape (#784).
- Update custom training stages to the three-stage pipeline. Configured plugins use a class with `from_config` (#754, #766).
- Update evaluation imports to `reef.evaluation` and shared contracts to `reef.core.evaluation` (#785).
- The legacy `reef.service.slime_driver` entry point and unused runtime APIs have been removed (#804).

See the [configuration reference](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/reference/configuration/) and [training pipeline guide](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/developer-guide/processors/) before upgrading custom deployments or recipes.

## What's Changed
* fix(service): route requests to a checkpointed release's adapter by @MikeZheng777 in https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/709
* fix(artifact): publish releases with relative work directories by @YihongT in https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/712
* fix: reject proposals exceeding the requires limit by @jane-jhu in https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/713
* Say when a grounding document was cut short by @Kaustubh1235 in https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/714
* chore(deps-dev): bump the python-minor-and-patch group with 2 updates by @dependabot[bot] in https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/716
* chore(deps): bump the docs-site-minor-and-patch group in /docs/site with 6 updates by @dependabot[bot] in https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/717
* chore(deps): bump virtualenv from 21.7.12 to 21.7.13 by @dependabot[bot] in https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/719
* fix(slime): honor training.timeout-s for worker RPCs by @GGQ1996 in https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/715
* Publish four Guidance-TTT paper solutions and evaluation commands by @Chonghe-Jiang in https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/720
* Add Yihong Tang to the contributors list by @quao627 in https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/721
* docs: correct stale behavior claims in active documentation (#603) by @Yi-111-a in https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/699
* docs: add ASD-STE100-inspired agent writing guidance by @BobbyZhouZijian in https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/724
* feat(train): put the trainer behind the InferenceEngine contract and let Slime publish to vLLM over the disk transport by @ruizhang0101 in https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/710
* refactor(harness): split adapter quirks into AdapterRenderer steps by @yanxz in https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/725
* fix(inference): retry SGLang and vLLM engine startup on port conflicts by @augustuszzq in https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/723
* fix(train): resume a run that never saved its optimizer, and keep its lr schedule by @MikeZheng777 in https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/728
* fix(sglang): start encoder-only engines through encode_server.launch_server by @augustuszzq in https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/731
* docs(operate): say what x-reef-release-id binds instead of promising a pinned version by @au

Infrastructure for continually self‑improving agents

[![CI](https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![PyPI package: reef-infra](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/reef-infra?label=PyPI%3A%20reef-infra&logo=pypi&logoColor=white)](https://pypi.org/project/reef-infra/) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12%2B-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)](pyproject.toml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-green)](LICENSE) English | [中文](README.zh.md)
Reef is the first open-source infrastructure for continual self-improving agents. It connects agent inference, feedback, learning, and versioned delivery. Use it to train model weights with Slime and SGLang, or improve an agent's harness, including its prompts, rules, and skills.
**🚀 [Get started](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/getting-started/quickstart/) | 🗺️ [Roadmap](https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/issues/25) | 🗓️ [Office Hours](https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/issues/818) | 📣 [Launch post](https://x.com/ao_qu18465/status/2094867930081337730) | 💬 [Join Discord](https://discord.gg/5y8e5f937k) | 📱 [Join WeChat Group](docs/community/wechat.md)**
## 📰 News - **2026-11:** We are refactoring Reef to a control plane + workers architecture. Some recipes and examples can fail on `main` until the refactor is complete. If a recipe fails, please [open an issue](https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/issues/new/choose). - **2026-11:** A scenario can split its traffic across its served artifacts [#1227](https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/1227), also through [Semantic Router](https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router) [#859](https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/859). The new `python` harness adapter evolves a Python program [#1242](https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/1242). - **2026-10:** Tinker runs as a training component [#901](https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/901). Episodes and agents can run in Modal Sandboxes [#942](https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/942). The artifact repository can live on Hugging Face [#1003](https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/1003). New recipe: [OPD](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/recipes/opd/) [#683](https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/683). - **2026-09:** [`reef-infra` v0.1.0](https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/releases/tag/v0.1.0) is on PyPI. New recipes: [GEPA](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/recipes/gepa/), [SDFT](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/recipes/sdft/), [SDPO](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/recipes/sdpo/) and [Meta-Harness](recipes/meta_harness/README.md). Reef serves the OpenAI Responses API at `/v1/responses` [#528](https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/pull/528). - **2026-08:** Reef is open source. Read the [launch post](https://x.com/ao_qu18465/status/2094867930081337730). ## 🎯 When to use Reef Use Reef when you want your agent to keep improving simply by learning from how you interact with your agent. | Your goal | Learning path | What you need | |---|---|---| | Keep getting stronger model designed for you | Model weight training | A trainable model, a supported GPU stack, and feedback your recipe can use | | Get your harness to self-improve | Harness optimization | A model endpoint, representative tasks, and an evaluator; no local training GPUs | | Scientific discoveries | Test-time training | An execution environment, a correctness checker, and a measurable objective | ## 🧩 How Reef fits your stack | Ability | Inference engine (vLLM, SGLang, …) | RL training framework (Slime, veRL, AReaL, …) | **Reef** | |---|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Serves live traffic | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | | Trains weights | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | | Version management | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | | Stays live through updates | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | | Evolves beyond weights (skills, harness) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ## 🔄 How it works
Reef processes each learning cycle in four steps. The table also shows which modules implement each step. | Step | What happens | Where it lives | |---|---|---| | **1 · Serve** | Serve agent requests and record interactions. | [`service/`](reef/service) — agent requests and interaction records
[`inference/`](reef/inference) — inference and artifact updates | | **2 · Observe** | Match feedback to recorded interactions. | [`storage/records.py`](reef/storage/records.py) — stored interactions and feedback
[`record2sample/`](reef/record2sample) — feedback matching, eligibility, and samples | | **3 · Grow** | Produce an update from eligible records. | [`recipe/`](reef/recipe) — recipe integration
[`train/`](reef/train) — the training pipeline, job data, and training jobs | | **4 · Commit** | Apply the configured selection policy and publish accepted updates. | [`evaluation/`](reef/evaluation) — candidate evaluation
[`artifact/`](reef/artifact) — version history and release components | ## 📦 Installation > 💡 **Note** > > Reef's artifact and checkpoint functionality requires the `git-lfs` system > package. Reef initializes Git LFS locally for its artifact repositories. We recommend [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for managing packages, and the commands below use it. ### From PyPI ```bash uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install reef-infra python3 -c "import reef; print(reef.__version__)" ``` ### From source ```bash git lfs install git clone https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef.git cd reef uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install -e . python3 -c "import reef; print(reef.__version__)" ``` Use the source checkout for development and for the training examples below. ## 🔧 Using Reef Reef supports two learning surfaces: model **weights** and agent **harnesses**. The deployment's recipe determines which surface its scenarios update. As a minimal example, start Reef as a pure inference server: ```bash uv run reef serve --inference.model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct ``` ### Weight-training deployment #### Start the deployment The following example starts the SAO (arXiv:2607.07508) example deployment. Run it from a Reef checkout in an environment that satisfies the GPU requirements in [Evolve your model](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/evolve-your-model/). ```bash uv pip install -e ".[slime]" && uv pip install --no-deps --group runtime export MODEL_PATH="Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct" export REEF_TOKEN="reef-local" reef serve -c recipes/sao/examples/imo_answerbench/serve.yaml \ --inference.model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \ --reef.port "8900" curl -f http://127.0.0.1:8900/healthz # ready to serve ``` #### Send an inference request and report feedback Send inference requests through Reef and report a score for each response. The SAO recipe uses each eligible scored rollout to run a training step. Reef's inference endpoint is OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible: `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses` and `/v1/messages` take the provider's own request body. A request includes the `x-reef-scenario` header; a new name creates a scenario using the deployment's configured recipe. Requests do not select recipes. The response body uses the provider's OpenAI-compatible format. Reef adds the `x-reef-agent-record-id` response header. Its value is the **receipt** that a later report uses to identify this interaction. A report can contain a numeric `score`, textual or structured `feedback`, and the receipts it evaluates. This example reports both a score and a short explanation. ```python import os import httpx reef = httpx.Client( base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8900", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['REEF_TOKEN']}", "x-reef-scenario": "hello-reef"}, timeout=300, ) # Send a provider-compatible inference request response = reef.post( "/v1/chat/completions", json={ "model": os.environ["MODEL_PATH"], "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Return exactly: reef is ready"}], }, ) response.raise_for_status() receipt = response.headers["x-reef-agent-record-id"] answer = response.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] # Sending report about the inference matched = answer.strip() == "reef is ready" reef.post( "/reef/report", json={"score": float(matched), "feedback": "matched" if matched else "wrong answer", "references": [receipt]}, ).raise_for_status() ``` `feedback` carries the richer signal, plain text or a structured object, for recipes that read more than a scalar. The endpoint will validate the **report schema** ([`reef/core/reports/`](reef/core/reports)). #### Watch it learn and grow Once the recipe has enough feedback, Reef submits a training job to the training component. When a checkpoint that the job saved passes evaluation, the inference runtime loads it as the new snapshot. Later inference requests use the current version without restarting Reef. ### Harness-evolving deployment Evolve a coding agent's skills and rules from scored feedback, using a model API instead of GPUs. A harness deployment serves `reef.recipe.harness:HarnessEvolutionRecipe`. The recipe keeps the agent harness as a tree of text files. At each step, a method edits a copy of that tree from the step's traces, the evaluation runs the real agent on tasks with the candidate, and a candidate that wins publishes as a snapshot that any client can pull. The [harness evolution tutorial](tutorials/evolve-your-harness/README.md) runs the smallest full loop on pi. It needs an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and Node.js and npm for pi. From your Reef checkout and activated Python environment: ```bash cd tutorials/evolve-your-harness ./run.sh ``` `configs/serve.yaml` names the endpoint (`inference.upstream-url`, no `/v1` suffix) and the model (`inference.upstream-model`). Edit them to point at your own provider, and set `REEF_UPSTREAM_API_KEY` if the endpoint needs a key. `run.sh` starts Reef on `127.0.0.1:8900`, sends the tasks through it, reports each score, and pulls the published tree. Each run writes `work/replay.html` with the snapshot chain and the files each step changed. `GET /reef/harness` serves the published tree, rendered for the deployment's adapter. The files carry no endpoint, key, or model: a client writes them where the agent reads them and binds the agent's model to this Reef (see [Use a published tree](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/evolve-your-harness/#use-a-published-tree)). Write the tree outside the project the agent works in: a session can write files in its project, so a tree there could change what the next session runs. [Evolve agent prompts, rules, and skills](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/evolve-your-harness/) explains the loop and its configuration. ## 📚 Recipes and examples Pick a recipe by the **task type** of your workload and by **what it should evolve**, model weights or the agent harness. Weight recipes need the GPU training stack, while harness recipes need only a model endpoint. Each recipe below links to its guide and each measured benchmark links to its results page, and the [recipe catalog](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/recipes/) adds the code and example for every recipe. [SFT](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/recipes/sft/) ships with `reef-infra` and trains on demonstrations or imported examples for every task type. The other implementations live in this repository's `recipes/` cookbook, selected by dotted class reference and not shipped in the Reef wheel. | Task type | Task shape | Evolves the model | Evolves the harness | Standard benchmarks | |---|---|---|---|---| | Open-ended discovery | Repeated attempts at one hard problem with a measurable objective and no known answer | [TTT-Discover](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/recipes/tttd/), [Guidance-TTT](recipes/tttd/examples/guidance_ttt/README.md) | None yet | Measured: [TriMul](recipes/tttd/examples/guidance_ttt/results/README.md), [circle packing](recipes/tttd/examples/tttd/README.md#formal-8x64-results), [Erdős minimum overlap](recipes/tttd/examples/tttd/README.md#formal-8x64-results). | | Offline tasks with a known answer | Independent tasks from a fixed set, each with a reference answer | [SAO](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/recipes/sao/), [SDFT](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/recipes/sdft/), [SDPO](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/recipes/sdpo/), [OPD](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/recipes/opd/) | [GEPA](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/recipes/gepa/), [Meta-Harness](recipes/meta_harness/README.md) | Measured: [IMOAnswerBench](recipes/sao/examples/imo_answerbench/README.md#results), [AIME 2024](recipes/opd/examples/math/README.md#results), [AIME 2025](recipes/gepa/examples/aime/README.md#the-validation-contract), [SciKnowEval](recipes/sdpo/examples/sciknoweval/README.md#results), [ToolAlpaca](recipes/sdft/examples/skill_stream/README.md#results), [Terminal-Bench](recipes/meta_harness/examples/terminal_bench/README.md#results). | | Online learning from usage | Sessions with a user, where the interaction itself is the signal | [OpenClaw-RL](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/recipes/openclawrl/) | [ACE](recipes/ace/README.md), [ReasoningBank](recipes/reasoning_bank/README.md) | Measured: [GSM8K with a simulated student user](recipes/openclawrl/examples/openclawrl/README.md#results). | [`recipes/basic/`](recipes/basic/) is the record-only starting stack and stays outside the catalog. For a small walkthrough of feedback, candidate edits, and publication, start with [the coding harness tutorial](tutorials/evolve-your-harness/README.md). Each result page documents its task, evaluation setup, measurements, and limitations. ## 📐 Architecture
## 📖 Learn more The [documentation](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/) is organized in the following order: - [Quickstart](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/getting-started/quickstart/): install Reef, connect a client, and inspect the version history - [HTTP API](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/reference/http-api/): use the HTTP API and report feedback - [Write a recipe](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/developer-guide/write-a-recipe/): configure how Reef processes data and produces updates - [Evolve your harness](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/evolve-your-harness/): evolve a harness instead of model weights - [Evolve your model](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/evolve-your-model/): configure and operate a training deployment - [Recipes](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/user-guide/recipes/): the catalog of cookbook recipes by task type, with code, docs, example, and results for each - [The core loop](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/getting-started/core-loop/): The core loop of Reef - [Glossary](https://reefinfra.ai/docs/reference/glossary/): Explanation of the terminologies used ## 🤝 Community & Contributing Working on continual self-improving agent? - [Join Discord](https://discord.gg/5y8e5f937k) to share your recipes, ask implementation questions, and discuss new features. - [Join the WeChat group](docs/community/wechat.md): the group is full, so add the assistant and it will invite you. - Join the [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/orgs/Human-Agent-Society/discussions) to ask questions, share ideas, and connect with the community. - Start contributing with the [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md). - Propose designs through an [RFC issue](https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/issues/new?template=rfc.yml). - Report suspected vulnerabilities privately by following the [security policy](SECURITY.md). If Reef looks useful to you, please give it a ⭐ — it helps the community to discover and contribute to the project. ## 📚 Citation If you use Reef in your research, please cite: ```bibtex @misc{reef2026, title = {Reef: Infrastructure for Continually Self-Improving Agents}, author = {{Reef Contributors}}, year = {2026}, url = {https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef} } ``` Citation metadata is also available in [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff). ## 👥 The Team Reef brings together people exploring how agents can learn from experience and improve over time. The people below help turn that idea into working infrastructure. This list is non-exhaustive, with team members listed alphabetically by last name: [Wenhao Chai](https://github.com/wenhaochai), [Shuangrui Ding](https://github.com/Mark12Ding), [Shiyi Zoe Du](https://github.com/zoedsy), [Hao He](https://github.com/hehaodele), [Haoze He](https://github.com/HectorHHZ), [Chonghe Jiang](https://github.com/Chonghe-Jiang), [Nan Jiang](https://github.com/nanjiangwill), [Xuan Jiang](https://github.com/Xuan-1998), [Xiaochen Li](https://github.com/SeuperHakkerJa), [Paul Liang](https://github.com/pliang279), [Bo Liu](https://github.com/Benjamin-eecs), [Boyuan Long](https://github.com/BoyuanLong), [Qiuyang Mang](https://github.com/joyemang33), [Zhenting Qi](https://github.com/zhentingqi), [Ao Qu](https://github.com/quao627), [Mingruo Qu](https://github.com/workhardforcoding), [Yihong Tang](https://github.com/YihongT), [Zhaokai Wang](https://github.com/wzk1015), [Xuezhi Yan](https://github.com/yanxz), [Hanfei Yu](https://github.com/hanfeiyu), [Haofei Yu](https://github.com/lwaekfjlk), [Simon Yu](https://github.com/simonucl), [Han Zheng](https://github.com/MikeZheng777), [Kaichen Zhou](https://github.com/kaichen-z), [Zijian Zhou](https://github.com/BobbyZhouZijian), [Jiacheng Zhu](https://github.com/Jiacheng-Zhu-AIML), [Dingyi Zhuang](https://github.com/ZhuangDingyi), [Xinkai Zou](https://github.com/jayzou3773). ## ⭐ Star History ## 🙏 Acknowledgements We are particularly grateful to these projects which power important parts of Reef: - [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) — high-performance inference - [slime](https://github.com/THUDM/slime) — model weight training
